data.narrative:
Fortera, a Series C-stage climate and energy company founded by Ryan Gilliam, has raised over $200M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 comparable companies—1 public (LNZA) and 8 private—including same-stage peers KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy, alongside later-stage players like Helion and Redwood Materials.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $200M total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C to next-stage advancement, implies a valuation of $340M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same-stage comparables yielded a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M (Amogy) to $3.0B (KoBold Metals). The wider peer range reflects heterogeneity in technology maturity and capital intensity within frontier climate tech.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $289M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $670M. The wide dispersion between stage-progression and peer-median methods—reflecting divergent assumptions about Fortera's competitive positioning relative to the peer set—represents the primary valuation uncertainty. Resolution hinges on technology differentiation, path to commercialization, and capital efficiency relative to comparables.
